Selected Work

I work on the parts of a game that make it feel less repetitive — NPCs with personality, quests with different objectives, dialogue that fits the character, and organized development work.

QUEST DESIGN

Quests That Aren't Just "Beat The Bandits"

I help with quests by making them diverse instead of making every quest the same bandit-beating mission. I like using NPC interactions, collecting, repairing, choices, exploration and rewards to give players different things to do.

ObjectivesRewardsNPCsVariety
Mechanic — Gunman Repair

A service quest where the player brings a damaged Gunman to a Mechanic. The repair costs 1 Gold Coin, giving the player a useful reason to interact with the NPC without turning the quest into another combat objective.

Barber — Change Your Look

A non-combat service interaction where the player can choose a hairstyle using a Hair ID. The haircut costs 5 Gold Coins, giving players another way to spend money and customize their character.

Why I design quests this way

I try to make quests feel different from each other. A game has more personality when players can repair something, meet an NPC, make a choice, collect something, explore an area or customize their character instead of always fighting enemies.

PROJECT MANAGEMENT

Keeping Development Organized

I like keeping game development clear and easy for the team to follow, from deciding what needs to be done to making sure features actually get finished.

RoadmapsTask PlanningDocumentationTesting

I break larger ideas into smaller tasks so everyone knows what they are working on. I keep track of priorities, write down important details and help connect the design side with the people actually building the feature.

I also think testing early is important. If something is confusing, repetitive or just doesn't feel fun, it is better to catch that while the feature is still being worked on instead of waiting until the whole game is finished.

My goal is simple: less confusion, clearer tasks and a game that keeps moving forward.

My Process

I try to keep the process simple so an idea can actually make it from a document into the game.

01

Start With The Idea

I figure out what the player is supposed to do, why it is worth doing and what makes the feature different from the rest of the game.

02

Build The Design

I write the NPC role, objectives, dialogue, rewards and other details so the feature has a clear direction before it gets built.

03

Organize The Work

I split the idea into tasks and keep track of what needs to be done by programmers, builders, artists or testers.

04

Test & Improve

I look for things that feel confusing, repetitive or unfinished and change them based on testing and feedback.
